hits.title: What is the capital of Japan? | Britannica
hits.snippet: The capital of Japan is Tokyo, one of the largest metropolitan areas in the world. It serves as the country's political, economic, and cultural center. Formerly known as Edo, the city became the imperial capital in 1868, replacing Kyōto, and today it is home to major government institutions, businesses, and many of Japan's leading cultural and educational organizations.

hits.snippet: The capital of Japan is Tokyo. [1][2][3] Throughout history, the national capital of Japan has been in locations other than Tokyo. The oldest capital is Nara.

hits.title: Tokyo - Wikipedia
hits.snippet: Tokyo, [a] officially the Tokyo Metropolis,[b] is the capital and most populous city of Japan . The population of the city proper was over 14 million as of 2023. The Greater Tokyo Area, which includes Tokyo and parts of six neighboring prefectures, is the third-most populous metropolitan area in the world, with 33 million residents as of 2025. hits.title: Tokyo Facts | Britannica
hits.snippet: Tokyo, the capital of Japan , is situated at the head of Tokyo Bay on the Pacific coast of central Honshu. First developed into a city during the Tokugawa period (1603-1867), when the site was known as Edo, Tokyo is the core of the Tokyo-Yokohama Metropolitan Area, commonly called Greater Tokyo. The city is Japan's major cultural centre as well as its main transportation hub.
